newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's quota-based poultry sector eyes exports.
newsitem.headline: Canada's quota-based poultry sector eyes exports.

text.p: Canada's quota-based poultry sector on Sunday began allowing packers and producers to enter into export oriented contracts, officials said.
"It allows our packers to be more (export) market responsive," Chicken Farmers of Canada marketing agency spokeswoman Nicole Beauchamp told Reuters.
Packers used to export any excess supply during each eight week marketing period. Now packers may contract supplies from producers specifically for export purposes, Beauchamp said.
Canada exported 31.7 million kgs (70 million lbs) of chicken in 1996 versus 33 million kgs in 1995, she said.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said the policy change may herald a new era of export oriented output.

"Poultry and dairy have been focused at the domestic market under the umbrella of supply management but the poultry industry is obviously becoming more interested in the potential for international opportunities," Goodale said.
Canadian chicken production in the last eight week marketing period ended March 15 totalled 112.79 million kgs (248.5 million lbs), figures show. Exports were not detailed.
About 2.37 million kgs (5 million lbs) of Canada's chicken output from now to May 15 is set for export markets, she said.
Canada exported chicken products to Russia, South Africa, Cuba and China in 1995. Figures were not available for 1996.
Goodale, who is on a 10-day trade mission to Japan and Indonesia with 50 business and government officials, said he hoped to boost trade in processed Canadian agrifood.
Canada exported C$18.8 billion in raw and processed food in 1996, up 39.3 percent from 1993's C$13.5 billion in exports. Goodale's target for the year 2000 is C$20 billion.
